look_here_first: POVERTY DROPSEED (*Sporobolus vaginiflorus*): SEE attached fibrous ROOTS and flowering stems on Bob Harms SPVA-b1 (gallery panel 1); then actual terminal and upper-sheath flower cluster positions on SPVA-i (panel 4). True grass hair ligule is an extremely short inner fringe, not a long membrane. NEW 2026 credited Commons anatomical plates in panels 13–14 show labelled LOWER/UPPER GLUMES, LEMMA and PALEA of a 3–5mm single-floret spikelet with 3mm/5mm photographed scale. Those photographer-identified European images are diagnostic teaching references, NOT proof of a Hays specimen or resolution of the S. ozarkanus/neglectus rank complex. Keep fully enclosed cleistogamy and 400× lemma hooks/hairs as separate required verification.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays long-term flora; Travis Balcones Canyonlands Preserve; Williamson County treatment.

best_field_traits: very narrow leaves about 1–2 mm wide
crew_field_check: Usually small, slender annual dropseed with narrow contracted terminal and axillary panicles; cleistogamous spikelets can hide high in the sheath. Size, annual root base and true mature lemma/spikelet measures together separate it from perennial S. compositus and S. clandestinus. The two current source-labelled photos do not show a diagnosable hidden flower.
1-flowered, awnless Sporobolus spikelets — not the multi-flowered bristled clusters of Setaria/Cenchrus.
Photographs of head outline are first clues, NOT confirmed lemma/pericarp identification.
Anther/flower color, panicle width and small/large height alone are not safe identifications.
crew_diagnostic_photo_second_pass_202610: 1. REAL ROOTED BASE: see author SPVA-b1 entire plant from fine fibrous roots to the upper narrow panicle, with source-scaled spikelet inset; the original unrooted small tuft alone never proves annual versus perennial duration.
2. PHOTO HABIT: author SPVA-a3 is actual small growth on rocky low vegetation, but far-away grass tufts are not sufficient as diagnostic ID.
3. FOLLOW ONE CULM: use author SPVA-c to locate consecutive true leaf SHEATHS and growing upper stem/leaf attachments; don't mislabel dead papery sheath tissue as reproductive units.

4. TERMINAL vs SHEATH: author SPVA-i shows the long narrow terminal seedhead AND separate shorter close-to-upper-sheath spikelet cluster lower on the culm. The existence of axillary inflorescence by itself does not certify the enclosed floral structures are self-fertilizing.

5. FLOWERING vs SEED: use SPVA-J1 genuine dark purple exserted structures along the spikelets and real scale; without reliable actual pixel dissection do not assign each individual colored appendage to anther/stigma.

6. TRUE SPIKELET DETAIL: SPVA-j2 shows narrow green/purple spikelet bracts with photographer scale; Sporobolus has one floret per spikelet. Mature glumes/lemma/palea must be separately identified from a detached specimen, not their colors alone.
7. DISARTICULATION: use source SPVA-d to identify the location of aging overlapping floral units; breaking above glumes and surface micromorphology remain separate microscopy tasks.

8. REAL SHORT LIGULE: SPVA-L source collar macro shows blade vs sheath; Gibson Williamson County treatment describes two-tier SHORT HAIRS approx. 0.1–0.3 mm. Do not claim a clearly photographed long membrane or invent arrow to individual tiny hairs.

9. COMPARE three installed Sporobolus: perennial rough (S. clandestinus) and composite (S. compositus) similar narrow panicles but persistent crowns; photograph fresh basal structures and true spikelets to avoid wrong ID.

10. FINISH CHECK: photo a local live same-plant rooted flowering/axillary material with explicit 1mm ruler, upper sheath lifted to expose a true cleistogene, disconnected mature glume vs lemma/palea grain; take 400× verified lemma hook/hair comparison for neglectus/ozarkanus and review mobile arrow endpoints.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Dig or expose anchored basal/rooted plant and compare fertile panicles and small mature spikelets.
field_matrix.difference: S. clandestinus is perennial with a very tight upright panicle; juvenile plants and drought conditions confuse stature.
field_matrix.guardrail: Tuft shape alone is not lifetime evidence.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Compare persistent crown, spikelet sizes and presence of upper-sheath flowering.
field_matrix.difference: S. compositus typically persists as perennial and can have enclosed self-pollinated spikelets too; simple presence of cleistogenes does not settle this ID.
field_matrix.guardrail: Separate S. neglectus/ozarkanus where small annual dropseed traits overlap; exact lemma study may require scope.

not_reliable_alone: Presence of hidden sheath flowers (multiple related dropseeds can have these)
Being taller/shorter or open/contracted at a single drought-stressed moment
Claiming a micro-lemma character from an ordinary phone photograph

field_id_finish_pass.stage: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — eight physically stored real documented Harms Texas botanical anatomy images now cover rooted habit, sheaths, head architecture, blooming, dispersal and collar; missing measured 1mm isolated lemma/callus/ligule and source-vouchered local microscope series.
field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: Poverty dropseed now has 13 exact-species locally archived photographs including an authentic rooted Harms Central Texas plant, terminal plus upper-sheath flowering architecture, original Harms collar, and NEW photographer-labelled measured 3mm and 5mm glume/lemma/palea macro references from Austrian *Sporobolus vaginiflorus* sensu Fischer et al 2008. These excellent photos support crew recognition and gross reproductive anatomy but do not settle local Hays county provenance, narrow ozarkanus/neglectus rank, true tiny inner ligule or microscopically confirmed lemma hooks/hairs. Preserve remaining scientific holds and image-specific rights/attribution.
photo_targets: REMAINING local same-voucher complete sequence: Hays authenticated rooted annual, entire attached flowering head, upper-sheath closed flowering position, leaf collar and fresh mature spikelet with own physical 1mm bar. Earlier Harms rooted plate is real but has no independent Hays voucher.

TRUE INNER LIGULE: photograph free inner 0.1–0.3mm hair fringe from open sheath with 20–40× and calibrated sub-millimeter bar. Existing Harms and new exterior collar photos show true junction but not individual inner hair lengths.
CLEISTOGAMY: before-and-after photographs of same unopened upper sheath with a truly concealed developed flower exposed, vouchered species; no assumption from separate near-sheath heads.

MICROSCOPIC COMPARISON: match 35–60× pubescent lemma and 400× hooks, microhairs, prickle/silica vs verified S. neglectus and ozarkanus at same maturity, under clearly documented microscope calibration and photo permissions.

SOURCE-DIFFERENTIAL NOTE: newly installed 3mm/5mm measured author-labelled gross glume/lemma/palea Austrian references (sl125/sl126) already cover general spikelet structure; do NOT claim their location establishes local Texas identity.

PUBLIC QA: verify all 15 gallery photos, per-image Stefan CC BY-SA4 adaptation/creator details and eight Harms educational-credit notices in rights-filtered website/mobile, arrow overlays and page build.

verified_published_characteristics.life_cycle: Tufted ANNUAL (FNA and Kew); existing rooted photo by itself does not prove full lifecycle
verified_published_characteristics.panicles: Terminal plus axillary narrow contracted heads, upper heads may be partly enclosed in sheaths
verified_published_characteristics.reproduction: Cleistogenes (cleistogamous florets) present in upper sheaths; seeing an external spikelet cluster is not direct proof of a closed flower
verified_published_characteristics.spikelets: 3–5 mm long and ONE fertile floret; lemma 3–5 mm and PUBESCENT (GrassBase)
verified_published_characteristics.ligule: Short HAIR FRINGE, FNA 0.1–0.3 mm; conflicting regional vegetative account says 1.0–1.5 mm, so require vouchered photograph and treat local measurement as unresolved

photographic_teaching_sequence: Harms SPVA-b1 shows genuine whole rooted herbaceous specimen; annotation still not proof of annual life history
Harms SPVA-i shows terminal and upper-sheath flowering positions; do NOT label enclosed flowers 'confirmed cleistogamy' without opening tissue
Harms SPVA-J1/J2 show actual flowering parts and scaled bract view; no unsupported single glume/lemma labels
Harms SPVA-L shows blade sheath junction; no micrometer hair fringe endpoints supported
lane4_20261023.comparison: S. neglectus usually shorter spikelets and glabrous fertile lemma; S. vaginiflorus has ~3–5 mm spikelets and pubescent lemma in classic treatments. S. clandestinus and S. compositus generally perennial. Compare fine pubescence and exact ripe glumes, not habitat or head narrowness alone.

0.1–0.3 mm inner ligule hair fringe under 20–40× and fine graduated reference, reconcile conflicting vegetative account
Safely documented truly enclosed cleistogamous floral unit in opened upper sheath, not inferred from near-sheath head

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Poverty dropseed — real rooted plant, upper-sheath flowering and ciliate ligule location
steps: ACTUAL ROOTS: Bob Harms SPVA-b1 in panel 1 (index 0) physically connects fine fibrous roots, leafy basal crown and several flowering culms. Its author's taxon ID is recorded, but site-specific Hays voucher and the full annual lifecycle are not established by one photograph.

TWO FLOWERING POSITIONS: SPVA-i at panel 4 (index 3) genuinely shows terminal panicle plus upper-sheath/axillary flowering heads on a culm. Closed self-fertilizing flowers have NOT been dissected, so do not infer cleistogamy from the exterior.

GROSS ANATOMY LEAP: New CC BY-SA4 author-labelled panel 13 (index 12) shows lower/upper glume, lemma and palea at 3-mm scale; panel 14 (index 13) shows eight angles at 5-mm scale. See these BEFORE teaching 400× lemma microscopy. Original annotations already belong to author; no new arrows added.

SHORT LIGULE: panels 8 and 15 (indices 7,14) show true sheath/collar locations, with the new exterior five-angle photograph having a 10-mm bar. The 0.1–0.3-mm INSIDE free fringe of hairs remains below photographically reliable resolution.

LOOK-ALIKES: panel 11 (index 10) is *S. clandestinus* and panel 12 (index 11) is *S. compositus*, BOTH DIFFERENT TAXA. Comparing head silhouettes alone will fail. Critical *S. neglectus* and *S. ozarkanus* comparison photo series remains absent.

FIELD FINISH: Photograph a locally authenticated same-plant root/flower/collar/spikelet with physically measured 0.1-mm hair-fringe macro and micromorphology of lemma hairs/hooks; open one upper sheath to expose genuinely concealed flower (not assumed from tuft).

Source attribution: Stefan.lefnaer, October 2026 Lower Austria photos are exact file individually licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and resized/EXIF-stripped; must maintain author/source/license/share-alike and adaptation note. Eight Bob Harms Monocots originals remain copyrighted and educational-credit only.
Do NOT change local BONAP county/native or accepted rank solely from Austrian reference images. Public Pages and mobile overlay placement still require separate live QA.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Use visible macro morphology first and defer difficult perennial-species separations to mature material, reliable grain tests and microscope when necessary.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: 13 physically archived EXACT SPECIES JPEGs (8 Harms, 2 earlier local, 3 new Stefan), plus 2 other species look-alike panels, 15 total gallery. One historical illustration remains remote outside gallery. Critical scientific holds: tiny 0.1–0.3mm inner true ligule, proof of enclosed upper-sheath floret, true 400× hairs/hooks vs S. neglectus/ozarkanus, local vouchered specimen, live Pages validation.

The sheath exterior is visible in panel 3 (index 2). However, a mature floret still hidden *inside* an unopened sheath and a true self-pollination event are NOT documented in these pixels. A botanist-confirmed dissection before-and-after opening a sheath of one authenticated plant remains the required high-value photograph.

field_id_short_tiles.short: Pubescent lemma matters more than head outline
field_id_short_tiles.details: Existing gallery panel 11 (index 10) is *S. clandestinus* and panel 12 (index 11) is *S. compositus*, both different species and generally perennial. New measured spikelet photos 13–14 (indices 12–13) show Austrian source-defined *S. vaginiflorus* anatomy, NOT same-maturity Texas *S. neglectus* or *S. ozarkanus*. S. neglectus may share annual tuft and hidden upper-sheath flowers but has smaller spikelets, often ~1.5–3 mm, and largely hairless lemma/palea in classical treatments. The ozarkanus taxon/rank has active scientific conflicts: preserve canonical taxonomy holds and demand vouchered lemma pubescence/veins before split.
